digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate T1 / web-search capability routing
propositions: Bedrock-qualified Claude models failed to receive the server-side web-search tool that T1 requires, because _anthropic_web_search_capabilities gated on provider-name prefix resolved.startswith('anthropic'), and bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 does not match that prefix.
The capability withdrawal was silent: provider_provenance.capabilities did not record that web access was withheld, so blocked plan reviews appeared grounded when they were not.

Gating web-search attachment on provider-name prefix violates the epic's standing rule of provider qualification by registry membership, not prefix matching, and that rule is enforced by an attested guard in the capabilities module.

T1 is a blocking criterion whose correctness depends on server-side web-search grounding; degrading it to codebase-only reasoning without warning creates a measurable fidelity gap between Anthropic and Bedrock providers, contradicting the first-class parity claim.

The fix relocates the decision from anthropic_model.py to capabilities.py, removes the prefix gate entirely, derives web-search attachment from model profile membership in supported_native_tools, and records the outcome (native/local/off) in provider_provenance.capabilities so future silent withdrawals are impossible to miss.

Where a provider lacks native server-side web search, rebar now supplies local fallback search via duckduckgo_search_tool, bounded by volume and shape constraints that the original provider-side-only design was protecting against, and the T1 rubric asserts web access is guaranteed rather than optional.
